from wordfreq import count
print(count('x² 2'))" && mkdir -p slice/001-wordfreq/review && cat > slice/001-wordfreq/review/S1.md <<'EOF'
# Review S1: Count the words of a text

- minor: [requirement] src/wordfreq.py:14 Lower-casing the whole text before matching can split one word in two: "İstanbul" lowers to "i" + combining dot + "stanbul", and the combining mark is not a letter, so `count` gives {"i": 1, "stanbul": 1} (D2, I2). Fix: find the words in the original text first, then lower-case each match, e.g. `Counter(w.lower() for w in _WORD.findall(text))`.
- minor: [requirement] src/wordfreq.py:9 `[^\W\d_]` is not exactly "a letter": it also takes non-decimal number characters such as "²" or "Ⅻ", so "x²" counts as the word "x²" (D2, I2). Fix: if strict letters matter, filter matches with `str.isalpha`-based logic (e.g. match `[^\W_]` runs plus apostrophes and split on non-alpha), or note the accepted gap.
EOF
cat slice/001-wordfreq/review/S1.md
input.description: Probe digit case and write review
